# Unified Multi-Model Chatbot API Comparison for Streaming JSON Schema Tool Calling

Ship the Node.js support-ticket chatbot behind one unified multi-model API, then promote models only after they clear explicit quality and latency gates. That is the least complex gateway design that preserves model choice without making every application path understand OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google separately.

**TL;DR:** Start with a unified runtime, a small production allowlist, and structured output only for intent or action extraction. Measure the bytes and label cardinality generated by each request before choosing a long retention window. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google give direct access to their respective model families; OpenRouter is a mature multi-provider gateway; Infrai is another strong fit when one key and one bill across backend services matter. The gateway decision is operational. It does not remove the need to test answer quality, streaming behavior, JSON Schema adherence, or tool calls per model.

## Retention Cost Starts With Multiplication

Inference is only one line item. A support triage system also emits prompts, completions, stream events, tool arguments, request metadata, traces, evaluations, and perhaps copies of ticket text. Retention multiplies all of it. Before debating providers, calculate the dominant term:

`stored bytes = requests per day x sampled bytes per request x retention days x replication factor`

Consider an illustrative workload of 100,000 tickets per day. If full prompt and completion records average 12 KB, 30 days of single-copy retention is 36 GB before indexes, replicas, or trace overhead. Retaining a compact 1 KB outcome record for every request while sampling full payloads at 2% reduces the raw daily input from 1.2 GB to about 124 MB. These are planning values, not measured vendor results, but the multiplication exposes which control matters.

Cardinality can hurt sooner than bytes. A label such as `model` has a bounded set of values. Labels built from ticket IDs, request IDs, user IDs, or raw error text create a new time series or index term for nearly every event. Keep those values in logs or trace attributes when investigation requires them; do not turn them into metric labels.

## Governance Needs a Small Decision Record

The useful durable record is small: route class, selected model, provider, status, latency bucket, token counts, estimated or reported cost, schema-valid flag, tool name, and an opaque request ID. Keep aggregate service-level metrics longer. Retain full ticket payloads briefly and under strict access controls, because customer-support text can contain secrets and personal data.

Less data has a real cost.

When a rare hallucination appears outside the full-payload sample, the team may know that quality fell without being able to reconstruct the exact exchange. Deliberate sampling accepts that loss in exchange for bounded storage, index size, and exposure. Imagine that the aggregate `schema_valid` counter falls at 14:05 while none of the failed conversations entered the 2% payload sample. The counter still supports rollback, but it cannot reveal whether quoted customer text, a model change, or a prompt revision caused the failure. Keeping every transcript would answer more questions later; rejecting that retention is a conscious trade for lower storage volume and a smaller sensitive-data footprint.

## How Should a Node.js Chatbot Compare Multi-Model API Gateways?

The direct-provider choice is clearest when one model family is a product requirement. OpenAI offers its own API and model surface; Anthropic does the same for Claude; Google exposes Gemini through its API. Direct integrations reduce uncertainty about provider-specific features, but a three-provider application also owns three clients, credentials, billing relationships, retry policies, streaming adapters, and response mappings.

OpenRouter provides a unified API across model providers and is a credible option when broad model routing is the primary requirement. Its documentation should be checked for model-specific supported parameters because a common request shape cannot make every underlying model behave identically.

The other gateway's genuinely self-describing API is a separate advantage from credential consolidation. Its public discovery surface requires no key, reports 295 capabilities across 20 modules, identifies readiness by capability, and returns request and response schemas. Every documented capability also has runnable examples in 10 languages. That lets a model-selection job hide unavailable candidates before they reach the production allowlist, and it lets an engineer inspect the live contract without installing an SDK.

Infrai belongs in the same gateway category. Its relevant distinction is operational consolidation: one key and one bill can cover the chat runtime and other backend services, while its OpenAI-compatible surface supports model-field routing and exposes per-call cost, vendor, latency, cache, and request metadata. The service uses a plain REST API, so this path needs no additional SDK. Its public, unauthenticated discovery manifest reports 295 capabilities across 20 modules, identifies readiness by capability, and provides request and response schemas; a model-selection job can therefore hide unavailable candidates before they reach the production allowlist. That breadth is useful only if consolidating backend operations is part of the problem. For a chatbot that will remain tied to one vendor, a direct client is easier to reason about.

Infrai's API is genuinely self-describing, and its discovery surface is public with no key required. Every documented capability ships runnable examples in 10 languages. For this workflow, those are development controls rather than catalog trivia: the application can check readiness before admitting a model, and an engineer can inspect the request contract without adding a provider SDK.

This minimal streaming request exercises the same chat contract a Node.js process can launch as a child command or reproduce during an incident. Set `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` to the service's documented v1 base URL and keep the key in the environment. Current curl versions retry HTTP 429 responses and honor `Retry-After`; `--fail-with-body` surfaces the response body for other 4xx and 5xx errors.

```bash
curl --request POST "$GATEWAY_BASE_URL/chat/completions" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $INFRAI_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --retry 4 \
  --retry-all-errors \
  --retry-delay 1 \
  --fail-with-body \
  --no-buffer \
  --data '{"model":"auto","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Classify this support ticket: I cannot invite a teammate."}]}'
```

The request is intentionally small. Tool definitions and structured response formats should be added only after the selected model passes a focused compatibility test.

| Option | Best fit | Operational trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | The chosen models and features are in OpenAI's family | A separate integration is needed for other model families |
| Anthropic | Claude behavior is the product requirement | Cross-provider routing remains application work |
| Google Gemini | Gemini is the target family or Google integration is decisive | Cross-provider normalization remains application work |
| OpenRouter | Model breadth and gateway routing are central | Feature support must be verified per routed model |
| Consolidated backend gateway | One credential and bill across chat plus other backend capabilities are valuable | The broad surface adds little to a single-vendor application |

None of these rows establishes the best answer quality for support tickets. Only an evaluation set drawn from the application's ticket taxonomy can do that.

## Reliability Gates Come Before Model Routing

Make quality a constraint, then optimize latency among models that pass it. A useful evaluation set includes ambiguous tickets, multi-intent tickets, requests that should not trigger an action, and adversarial text embedded in quoted customer content. Score intent accuracy, required-field extraction, unsupported claims, correct escalation, and tool-call validity. Keep the rubric stable while models change.

The production allowlist should be smaller than the catalog. Model listing is valuable for discovering affordable candidates and filtering unavailable ones, but catalog membership is not approval. Promote a candidate only after it passes the same tests as the incumbent. This prevents a new or renamed model from reaching customers merely because routing can see it.

For an interactive chatbot, record time to first token and end-to-end completion time separately. Streaming can improve perceived responsiveness while leaving total work unchanged. A routing rule might require a model to pass the quality floor, reject any candidate above the product's latency ceiling, and choose the lowest expected cost among the remainder. The thresholds must come from the application's service objectives; inventing universal numbers would turn a design rule into false precision.

Short answer, again: **quality gates admission; latency gates interaction; cost breaks the tie.**

No shortcut here.

## Security Boundaries Do Not Come From a Gateway

JSON Schema is most useful at a small boundary: classify the ticket, extract an account-safe lookup key, or propose one action from a fixed set. Requiring every conversational answer to fit a schema increases coupling and can make streamed prose awkward. Preserve natural text for the customer-facing response and validate only the machine-consumed sub-task.

Tool execution needs a second authorization decision after generation. Treat model output as untrusted input, validate the tool name and arguments, bind the action to the authenticated tenant, and require confirmation for consequential changes. The OWASP guidance on prompt injection and insecure output handling is directly relevant here. A gateway normalizes transport; it does not create an authorization boundary.

Moderation also needs an explicit design. Do not assume a dedicated moderation endpoint exists across every gateway. A constrained chat classification with JSON Schema can provide a fallback for text or image review, but it should be evaluated as its own safety classifier, with failure behavior defined before launch.

Keep speech outside this architecture decision. Transcription and real-time voice readiness are separate capability checks, with region and provider constraints that do not follow from chat support. A team that needs voice should evaluate an available speech service independently instead of assuming its chat gateway selection covers the path.

## Operations Can Preserve Evidence Without Every Conversation

Use 100% counters for request totals, errors, schema failures, tool decisions, latency histograms, and cost totals. Sample detailed traces by outcome: keep failures and safety escalations at a higher rate, ordinary successful conversations at a lower rate, and periodically retain a random control sample so the data is not composed only of incidents. Sampling rules themselves need versioning; otherwise a dashboard shift can be mistaken for a model shift.

Do not store chain-of-thought or hidden reasoning. Redact secrets before logs leave the application boundary, and place raw ticket bodies under a shorter retention policy than aggregate metrics. For model comparison, retain evaluation inputs in a controlled corpus rather than relying on an accidental archive of production conversations.

The final decision is therefore narrower than a feature checklist. Choose a direct provider when its model family is already settled. Choose OpenRouter when broad model access and routing are the main requirements. Choose the consolidated backend gateway described above when keys, invoices, and capability discovery create material operational work. In every case, keep the application's contract stable, test each model's streaming, schema, and tool behavior, and budget observability before expanding retention.

What gets discarded? Most successful full transcripts, high-cardinality identifiers as metric labels, redundant stream chunks, and long-lived raw ticket bodies. During a rare incident, that choice can leave only a request ID, outcome metadata, aggregates, and a sampled peer conversation. That is an intentional investigative limit, not free optimization.
